items.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: In 1946, that was the same year that Marisol created his famous quartet in the conservatory, so that can be easily the second one in the history of the saxophone.

ctx.x: How did your father go about developing himself as a musician?

I have no idea; he never talked much about that. I know that he got interested in classical music and the development of the classical saxophone in Cuba. He imported the— because there is a picture—he imported the French school of saxophone in 1946, all the books from a classical saxophone place in Paris to Havana in 1946. So, he created a group called “Cojuntos Symphonicos en Saxophones” –Symphonic Ensemble of Saxophones. In 1946, that was the same year that Marisol created his famous quartet in the…
So your father in addition to learning to play the instrument, he actually sold the instruments as well.
